chunks: He was asked about a man who comes to the mosque while they are in salat (prayer), and the Imam has preceded him by one rak'ah. So he pronounces takbir, then the Imam becomes unable to continue, takes his hand, and since he is the nearest of the people to him, he puts him forward.

So he عليه السلام said: “He completes the salat (prayer) with them, then sits until, when they have finished the tashahhud, he gestures with his hand to the right and the left; and that one’s gesturing with his hand is the taslim, or their prayer is completed, and he completes what he had missed.”

key_terms.التَّشَهُّدِ: the sitting testimony recited near the end of the prayer
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: the ritual salat (prayer) being performed in congregation
key_terms.الْإِمَامُ: the prayer leader of the congregation
key_terms.الْمَسْجِدَ: the mosque, where the congregational salat is taking place
key_terms.بِرَكْعَةٍ: by one rak'ah, meaning one unit of prayer had already passed for the latecomer
key_terms.فَاتَهُ: what he had missed from his own prayer before joining

ai.seo_question: What should a latecomer do if the Imam in congregational prayer becomes unable to continue and appoints him to lead?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for congregational salat (prayer) when a latecomer is brought forward to replace an Imam who becomes unable to continue. It explains how he should complete the congregation’s prayer first, then make up the rak'ah he had missed.
